solution:
Using the addition formula,
$$\sin\left(n\pi+\tfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\sin(n\pi)\cos\tfrac{\pi}{3}+\cos(n\pi)\sin\tfrac{\pi}{3}=0+(-1)^n\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}(-1)^n.$$

Therefore the series is
$$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}(-1)^n}{2^n}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\left(-\frac12\right)^n.$$

This is a geometric series with first term $1$ and common ratio $-\tfrac12$, whose sum is
$$\frac{1}{1-(-\tfrac12)}=\frac{1}{\tfrac32}=\frac23.$$

Hence the value is
$$\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot\frac23=\frac{\sqrt3}{3},$$
which is **option C**.
hints: Simplify sin(nπ+π/3) using the addition formula to get (-1)^n √3/2.
This turns the series into a geometric series with ratio -1/2.
Sum the geometric series and multiply by √3/2.
